findings.text: ledger-db had infra deploy d-477 (instance type migration by noah) about 56 minutes before the first alert, a direct change just before the alert.
ledger-db's sync blast radius covers 10 alerting services but not kyc-svc, so it does not account for every alert and is weakened.
Page Noah Becker (on-call, resolved 3 ledger-db incidents) and Meera Iyer (resolved 4), both awake at the query time; Chris Walker is asleep.
Four past ledger-db incidents were connection-pool exhaustion from a config change, causing 5xx errors across the payments cluster; rollback resolved each in 5-9 minutes.
No change to ledger-svc itself appears before the alert; the only nearby change is upstream ledger-db deploy d-477, one hop away.
ledger-svc's sync blast radius covers billing, payments, payouts, refunds, mobile-bff, partner-api and web-gateway, but not audit-svc, kyc-svc or reporting-svc, so it is weakened.
History shows ledger-svc only as an affected service, not a root cause; the matching ledger-db incidents trace to ledger-db's pool config, not ledger-svc.
INC-121 was an fx-rates infra change that degraded dependent services with rising errors and latency, fixed by restarting fx-rates in 20 minutes.
No deploys or config changes to fx-rates in the 120 minutes before the first alert.
fx-rates' blast radius misses audit-svc, kyc-svc, ledger-svc and reporting-svc, and predicts orders-api and pricing-svc alerts that are absent, so it is weakened.
